headlines.full_text: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US. California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, changing them instead to life in prison. "We can now let these offenders die in obscurity while we forever remember and honour the victims," he said in a letter. The decision to spare death row inmates is largely symbolic in a state that has not executed an inmate since 2006, though experts say it could save millions of dollars in court costs each year. Only 13 inmates have been executed since voters reinstated the death penalty in 1978. The decision comes as Newsom, the Democratic leader of the most populous US state, has been discussed as a possible 2028 contender for president. Newsom, who is term limited, is winding down his final months in office. Fellow Democrat Xavier Becerra is projected to take over after the midterm elections on Tuesday. Newsom explained in his letter that he is exercising his constitutional clemency authority to commute the sentences to life without the possibility of parole. "After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom said. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system and diminishes each of us". headlines.full_text: IRGC downs two more US MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island TEHRAN – The Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) says its electronic warfare systems have brought down two more US-made MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island in southern Iran, bringing the number of such drones intercepted there to six. TEHRAN – The Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) says its electronic warfare systems have brought down two more US-made MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island in southern Iran, bringing the number of such drones intercepted there to six. In two statements issued on Thursday night, the IRGC said the fifth and sixth drones had been downed in the island’s airspace by advanced electronic warfare systems operated by its Aerospace Force. The announcement followed an earlier statement on Monday, in which the IRGC reported bringing down two other MQM-170 drones south of Qeshm Island, bringing the total number intercepted to four. Separately, the IRGC said its air defense systems had intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-9 drone over the eastern Strait of Hormuz. The force identified it as the 55th American MQ-9 drone brought down by its air defenses. According to the IRGC, the drone was engaged by a newly deployed air defense system operated by the Aerospace Force as part of Iran’s integrated air defense network.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece celebrates Iranian forces’ success in downing U.S. drones, portraying them as heroic.

At least 12 other military sites, including missile complexes and air bases, appear to show signs of repairs. New roofs have been built on destroyed buildings at the Kermanshah missile base in western Iran, near the border with Iraq, while damaged buildings and debris have been cleared at the Parchin military complex - which has been repeatedly repaired despite a succession of air strikes - east of the capital. headlines.full_text: Netanyahu accused of attempting ‘coup’ after election defeat Israeli politicians and commentators have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of attempting a coup after his election defeat on Oct. 27, which followed a historic turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. Israeli politicians and commentators have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of attempting a coup after his election defeat on Oct. 27, which followed a historic turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. They say he is using the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic intelligence agency, to undermine the result and retain power. More than a week after the results showed the Netanyahu-led bloc trailing the opposition, Shin Bet chief David Zini is reportedly leading investigations into the Palestinian vote. The inquiries have raised allegations of voting fraud, bribery and foreign interference, despite no evidence being made public. The investigations coincide with Netanyahu’s campaign to delegitimize the Palestinian-led parties Ra’am and the Joint List, which together secured an unprecedented 19 seats in the Knesset. Critics say the effort is aimed at keeping him in power. On Tuesday, the Shin Bet arrested Middle East Eye contributor Abd Abu Shahadeh, citing a “security-related investigation”. Israeli media reported that Zini also wants Palestinian political leaders Ahmad Tibi, Sami Abou Shahadeh, Mansour Abbas and Ayman Odeh questioned. Yair Golan, leader of the opposition Democrats party, warned on Wednesday that Israeli democracy was under threat. “The police are detaining political activists without a warrant. The Shin Bet is trying to question senior elected officials without presenting evidence. The outgoing government refuses to recognize the election results,” he said.

US President Donald Trump said he had held phone conversations on Friday on the settlement in Ukraine and intends to continue them on Saturday, November 7. "I've had phone calls today. I'm having some tomorrow," he said in response to questions from journalists in Florida. The American leader did not specify with whom he discussed this topic.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article simply reports Trump's claim about phone talks on Ukraine without additional commentary or bias.

headlines.full_text: Trump sure Russia committed to resolving Ukrainian conflict The US president affirmed that Ukraine wants settlement as well WASHINGTON, November 7. /TASS/. Russia is committed to resolving the conflict in Ukraine, US President Donald Trump said. "Russia and Ukraine, for the first time, I think want settlement," he told journalists. Russia has repeatedly stated its readiness to negotiate the Ukrainian conflict. Speaking at Valdai on October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that the situation around Ukraine is not a matter of a "piece of land" for Moscow, but a matter of people. Russia needs to create conditions not for a truce, but for lasting peace, "for a long historical perspective"; Russia "needs security guarantees," Putin said.

headlines.title: Florida governor readies to run for president in 2028 — WP
headlines.full_text: Florida governor readies to run for president in 2028 — WP According to sources cited by the newspaper, Ron DeSantis has already approached at least one political consultant with a proposal to participate in his election campaign WASHINGTON, November 7. /TASS/. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is preparing to run in the 2028 US presidential election, according toThe Washington Post(WP). It quoted sources as saying that DeSantis plans to seek the Republican Party’s nomination and has already approached at least one political consultant with a proposal to participate in his election campaign. The political committee supporting the governor has begun raising funds. DeSantis’s supporters said he considered it possible to seek the highest office anew in light of the Republicans’ resounding failure in the November 3 midterm elections - the GOP will lose control over both houses of Congress, with the Democrats gaining a majority in both. Florida is among the states where the Republicans’ position remained strong. DeSantis participated in the 2024 presidential race but withdrew to support Donald Trump. Trump has previously said he sees current Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio as the ideal candidates to lead the country after his presidential term. He is sure that their tandem would be unbeatable in the 2028 election. Trump did not specify what position he would like to see each of them in. Vance did not rule out running for president in 2028.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article simply reports DeSantis's political plans without emotive framing.

headlines.title: UN Maritime Organization says 25 sailors died in Strait of Hormuz since February 28
headlines.full_text: UN Maritime Organization says 25 sailors died in Strait of Hormuz since February 28 The number of attacks on commercial vessels in the region stands at 130 LONDON, November 7. /TASS/. At least 25 sailors have died in the Strait of Hormuz during a conflict between the United States and Iran, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) of the United Nations said. According to the specialized UN agency with headquarters in London, the latest victim of the conflict, which has been going on since February 28, was a sailor from the tanker Velos Sapphire, attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on November 5. The number of attacks on commercial vessels in the region stands at 130, while thousands of sailors remain trapped in the Persian Gulf. Sailors continue to die and suffer serious injuries, to be left to fend for themselves, to lose the opportunity to return home, and to face shortages of essential supplies, including water, food, and medical care, as a result of the ongoing geopolitical conflicts, said IMO Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez. After a five·day meeting of the IMO Council, which ended on November 6, its members called on member states to refrain from unlawful actions that could jeopardize the safety of seafarers and international shipping. Dominguez also pledged to develop new measures that the organization could take to prevent further loss of life and mitigate the humanitarian consequences of the crisis.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article reports UN casualty figures factually, with no bias.

headlines.full_text: Dmitriev urges Europe not to worry after Kushner’s remarks about security architecture The presidential envoy accompanied his post with a screenshot of a Financial Times story, which quoted sources as saying that Jared Kushner’s comment about potential security agreements in Europe involving Russia came as a surprise to European officials MOSCOW, November 7. /TASS/. "Don't worry be happy," Dmitriev wrote on Instagram (banned in Russia, owned by Meta Corporation, recognized as extremist in Russia). He accompanied his post with a screenshot of aFinancial Times(FT) story, which quoted sources as saying that Kushner’s comment about potential security agreements in Europe involving Russia came as a surprise to European officials. Earlier, the FT said that EU member states are opposed to using peace talks on Ukraine to discuss a new security architecture. They also fear that the administration of US President Donald Trump may clinch a deal with Russia to the detriment of European security. On November 6, Kushner wrote on X that, according to the United States, potential security agreements in Europe involving Russia could include communication channels in crisis situations and a greater military transparency.

headlines.full_text: US envoy’s words on security architecture come as complete surprise to Europe — newspaper According to the newspaper, EU member states fear that US President Donald Trump’s administration might strike a deal with Russia that would undermine European security LONDON, November 6. /TASS/. headlines.raw_title: Europe must convince Russia that Ukraine won’t join NATO — French presidential candidate
headlines.title: Europe must convince Russia that Ukraine won’t join NATO — French presidential candidate
headlines.full_text: Europe must convince Russia that Ukraine won’t join NATO — French presidential candidate Nicolas Dupont-Aignan emphasized that the solution to the conflict should be long term rather than a temporary ceasefire MOSCOW, November 6. /TASS/. European countries must assure Moscow that Ukraine will not join NATO and that there will be no NATO forces on its territory, Nicolas Dupont-Aignan, a candidate in the 2027 French presidential election and leader of the Debout la France (Rise Up France) party, said during aVestibroadcast. He emphasized that the solution to the conflict must be long term rather than a temporary ceasefire. "That is precisely why it is very important for the Americans and Europeans to clearly state to Russia: NATO will never be in Ukraine. I believe European countries must assure Russia that Ukraine will not join NATO," Dupont-Aignan said, noting that Ukraine should not join the EU either. The politician also pointed out that Vladimir Zelensky does not want peace. "But he is not the only one. He is being pushed toward war by Ms. [European Commission President Ursula] von der Leyen, the EU’s military-industrial lobby, as well as German, UK, and French leaders," he added. Speaking about France’s continued financial support for Ukraine, Dupont-Aignan noted: "This is madness, suicide - after all, we’re talking about French taxpayers’ money. France has already allocated 25 billion euros to Mr. Zelensky, while we don’t have enough money for our hospitals, our schools and universities, or to lower fuel prices.".
headlines.llm_reasoning: He accuses *the EU's military-industrial lobby* of pushing war, framing institutions as corrupt.

headlines.full_text: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated. Tanzania's main opposition leader, Tundu Lissu, has been found guilty of inciting unrest and sentenced to four years in jail, in a case that has raised concerns about political freedom in the East African country. A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him of the more serious offence of treason, saying prosecutors had failed to prove a key element of that charge. But they said the 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, had encouraged his supporters to disrupt the disputed 2025 general election. Lissu, who leads the opposition Chadema party, has denied the charges, describing the prosecution as politically motivated. The court said his campaign slogan "No Reforms, No Election" was sufficient for him to be convicted of the charge of incitement. "By uttering those words with the intention of disseminating them to the public, the accused incited the public to disrupt the 2025 elections," the court ruled. Lissu said he had only been charged with treason, not incitement. "The offence of incitement is one that you, honourable judges, have manufactured. You have created an offence that did not exist, and you have done so on political directives," Lissu told the court. He added that he would like to apply for bail as this was possible for incitement, unlike treason. He has leave to appeal at the Court of Appeal - the country's highest court. Protesters gathered outside Poland’s top court as a long-running political dispute involving President Karol Nawrocki and Donald Tusk’s government escalated. (AP Video.) Friday’s late-night confrontation at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which drew riot police and protesters and prompted PresidentKarol Nawrockito turn his plane around and return to Warsaw, has reignited a bitter debate over whether Prime Minister Donald Tusk is restoring the rule of law or overstepping constitutional limits. headlines.full_text: Protests and reforms: France's rising debt costs threaten stability France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have? Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament. If, in response tonationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have. France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billioninvestment packagefor infrastructure and defense. Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook. As a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. headlines.full_text: France sees biggest day of protests in years About 575,000 protesters participated in demonstrations across France on Thursday, according to government estimates, marking the biggest single day of protests since a wave of unrest began in September to coincide with a nationwide strike. About 575,000 protesters participated in demonstrations across France on Thursday, according to government estimates, marking the biggest single day of protests since a wave of unrest began in September to coincide with a nationwide strike. Despite the scale of these protests, and the violence which marred similar marches on October 17, the day passed relatively peacefully, albeit with some localized clashes in cities across France, CNN reported. Some workers went on strike too, depleting some schools, universities, railways and, to a lesser extent, hospitals of their staff. The diverse nature of sectors involved reflects just how many groups are now participating in these protests, which have expanded from students demanding better conditions in schools to a movement that has drawn in trade unions and Yellow Vest protesters. Each group has its own concerns, though they are united by widespread discontent over the cost of living, perceived government inaction, a growing wealth divide and a deep desire for social and political change. Several of France s biggest unions, representing everyone from students, teachers and postal workers to doctors, pharmacists and transport workers had called for a nationwide strike on Thursday. About one in three of France s higher education institutions were disrupted because of the demonstrations, while about 13% of all school staff went on strike, the government estimated. Only Harwood, North Dakota, a small town with a population of fewer than 800 people, voted to oppose such limits. Russian-led team suspects volcanic activity on Mars A scientific study suggests that hydrogen chloride detected near Mars’ Alba Mons volcano could be seeping from underground magma chambers
Read Full Article at RT.com Mars may still have volcanic activity beneath its surface despite the absence of observed eruptions, a new Russian-led study suggests. Areas where volcanic gases continue to seep from underground could be promising locations to search for signs of life. The Red Planet bears extensive evidence of ancient volcanism dating back more than 3 billion years, when Olympus Mons, the largest known volcano in the solar system, began forming. Seismometers have also detected slight tremors known as ‘marsquakes’, but sulfur dioxide, a telltale sign of volcanic activity, has never been detected in the Martian atmosphere. An international team of researchers has linked unusual concentrations of another common volcanic gas, hydrogen chloride (HCl), detected by a Mars orbiter, to possible magmatic activity deep beneath the surface. HCl can indicate the presence of active magma chambers, although it can also be produced by chemical reactions in the atmosphere. The study, published in Science Advances on Wednesday, examines repeated HCl detections concentrated near Alba Mons, another ancient Martian volcano. The researchers suggest that gas escaping from underground magma could become trapped beneath ice during colder months before being released as temperatures rise in early summer. The gas was detected by the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO), a spacecraft developed jointly by the European Space Agency and Russia’s Roscosmos. Read Full Article at RT.com Two astronauts have ventured outside the International Space Station (ISS) to complete a major solar power upgrade, with NASA broadcasting live footage of the operation. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk began their spacewalk at 13:36 GMT on Thursday to install the station’s eighth and final roll-out solar array. The mission lasted 6 hours and 59 minutes and was successfully concluded at 20:35 GMT. The operation involved transporting a tightly packed solar panel across the station’s exterior, around 420 km above Earth. Menon rode the station’s robotic arm while carrying the equipment before joining Kutryk to secure it in place. Once the astronauts release the bolts holding the panel in its rolled-up position, it can unfurl on its own in around ten minutes. During the mission, the astronauts had also to contend with the station’s rapid transitions between daylight and darkness, which occur roughly every 45 minutes. Some electrical connections were completed during orbital night, when the existing arrays are not generating power. Last week’s spacewalk to install the station’s seventh solar array lasted 7 hours and 11 minutes. According to NASA, the upgrade will increase the ISS’ available electrical power by around 30%, from 160 to 215 kilowatts. German military convoy crashes in Poland Three German soldiers were hospitalized after two military trucks collided on a highway in Poland, military police say  
Read Full Article at RT.com Three German soldiers have been hospitalized after two military trucks traveling in a convoy collided with each other on a highway in southwestern Poland, the Polish Gendarmerie has said. The collision on the A4 highway near Kostomloty, 27 km from Wroclaw, left three German soldiers injured on Wednesday, military police spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Dariusz Rozkosz said. The drivers were sober, he added. The Polish authorities confirmed that the German military convoy was transiting through the country under a permit that does not require a Polish military escort. Its final destination was not disclosed. The crash caused major a traffic disruption, with lines stretching up to 10 km. Firefighters said the military vehicles were transporting around 150 liters of diesel fuel, although the container remained intact. Traffic restrictions were lifted later that day. This comes as Germany expands its military activities in Eastern Europe as part of NATO’s buildup along the eastern flank. Since June, German military engineers have been deployed to Poland to help construct the ‘Eastern Shield’, a network of fortifications along the border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad and Belarus. Berlin is also establishing a permanent military presence in neighboring Lithuania, where a German armored brigade is expected to become fully operational by the end of 2027. Information about "secret prisons" in the Ukrainian army has now become public because there are forces that want to replace Vladimir Zelensky, Alexander Dudchak, a leading researcher at the Institute of CIS Countries and an expert with the Other Ukraine movement, told TASS. Earlier, Ukrainian publication Strana said that such "prisons" have existed in the country since 2014. They appeared at the height of fighting in Donbass and are referred to in soldiers’ slang as "a pit." Initially, they were used for disciplinary violators in the army, and after 2022, mobilized individuals began to be sent there as well. Now, according to eyewitness accounts, torture and abuse are widely practiced in the "pits." According to Dudchak, information about this has been available for a long time. "There was talk about closed SBU prisons. And they weren’t really that closed," he explained. "The novelty is that all of this has entered the open information space. "There are forces that would like to replace Zelensky. Him personally, and his company. This, in general, reflects the struggle between various centers of influence over Ukraine." The expert had previously told TASS that the disclosure of information about the "prisons" could harm Zelensky and his entourage. According to Dudchak, they are "people-functions; they can be replaced," and the West needs to preserve the regime itself, not specific individuals.

The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said the cyberattack compromised monitoring and control systems operated by an external refrigeration supplier, allowing attackers to remotely manipulate temperature and defrosting settings at three plasma storage facilities. The hackers reportedly attempted to raise the temperature from the normal -30C (-22F) to as high as 110C (230F), well above the boiling point, according to French investigative weekly Le Canard Enchaine, which first reported the incident. The attack occurred overnight on Monday, when a technician on duty noticed temperatures rising inside the facilities. headlines.full_text: From New York, California to Idaho and Nebraska: Diwali's footprint growing across America Governors across five US states host their first-ever Diwali celebrations, while 22 cities in Washington State join the festivities Governors across five US states host their first-ever Diwali celebrations, while 22 cities in Washington State join the festivities Diwali is finding an increasingly prominent place in America's public life, moving beyond celebrations in Indian-American communities into state capitols, governors' residences, city halls and even the White House. The shift has gathered pace over the past two years. Pennsylvania became the first US state to designate Diwali as a state holiday in 2024, followed by legislative recognition in Connecticut and California in 2025. New York City, meanwhile, made Diwali a public school holiday in 2023. This year, the festival has made another significant leap. Governors of Idaho, Nebraska, Montana, North Dakota and Washington have hosted Diwali celebrations for the first time at state institutions, while more than 20 mayors have joined celebrations across the Pacific Northwest. The festivities are also reaching the country's most prominent political address, with US President Donald Trump scheduled to host a Diwali celebration at the White House. headlines.full_text: Nic Graham, Lakewood police agent, identified as officer killed in Colorado RTD bus shooting Lakewood police agent Nic Graham dies after a suspect opens fire on officers aboard an RTD bus in Colorado. A Lakewood police agent killed in a shootout with a suspect aboard a public transport bus inColoradohas been identified as Nic Graham. The seven-year department veteran was among four agents injured when the suspect opened fire on officers on Thursday, November 5. Lakewood Police Chief Philip Smith confirmed Graham's identity on Friday. Three other agents and a bystander were also injured in theshooting. The suspect was shot and killed by police at the scene. According to CBS Colorado, the incident began with a hit-and-run crash near Kipling and West 13th Avenue shortly before 3:45 pm on Thursday. The suspect reportedly fled the scene, but witnesses provided police with a description. “Witnesses at the scene told police that the suspect ran from the scene almost immediately, but they were able to get a good description of the suspect,” Lakewood Police Public Information Agent John Romero said. Several hours after the crash, a Lakewood police agent spotted the suspect boarding an RTD bus near Colfax Avenue and Wadsworth Boulevard at around 6:30 pm. When officers approached him, the suspect opened fire at approximately 6:32 pm. Police returned fire, hitting the man, who was pronounced dead at the scene. Four Lakewood police agents were taken to hospital with injuries ranging from serious to critical. Graham later died. One bystander was also injured and taken to hospital.
